title: Computing engines and control of VLMC with covariates
text: use household electricity consumption data set (powerconsumption, see also vignette("covlmc")), restricted fifth week discretised three states. covariate indicates whether measurement made day. select model AIC default engine (VGAM::vglm() time series three states): nnet::multinom(): two engines lead context tree, close likelihoods AIC. models shown coefficients, first VGAM::vglm(): nnet::multinom(): coefficients identical (displayed precision), ones high context different.

text: Since version 0.3.0, mixvlmc represents discrete time series objects class dts, created dts() function. dts stores time series together state space, .e. set values series can take. dts can built numeric, character, factor logical vector. state space specified, computed vector way depends type. numeric character vectors, state space consists unique values series, increasing order: factor, state space given levels factor, including levels appear series, order levels: logical vector, state space always c(FALSE, TRUE): default, first 5 values series printed, can changed n parameter print(): is_dts() tests whether object discrete time series, states() returns state space dts_data() recovers original series vector (type state space): length dts given length() dts can subsetted [. result dts state space, even states appear subset: Discrete time series contain missing values:
code: x_num <- dts(c(3, 1, 2, 2, 1, 3)) x_num #> Discrete time series of length 6 with state space 1, 2, 3 #>  3 1 2 2 1 ... states(x_num) #> [1] 1 2 3 x_chr <- dts(c("b", "a", "c", "a", "b")) states(x_chr) #> [1] "a" "b" "c" x_fct <- dts(factor(c("low", "high", "low"),   levels = c("low", "medium", "high") )) x_fct #> Discrete time series of length 3 with state space low, medium, high #>  low high low x_lgl <- dts(c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)) states(x_lgl) #> [1] FALSE  TRUE set.seed(0) x_long <- dts(sample(c("A", "B", "C"), 50, replace = TRUE)) x_long #> Discrete time series of length 50 with state space A, B, C #>  B A C A B ... print(x_long, n = 15) #> Discrete time series of length 50 with state space A, B, C #>  B A C A B A C C B B C C A A A ... is_dts(x_chr) #> [1] TRUE is_dts(c("b", "a", "c")) #> [1] FALSE dts_data(x_chr) #> [1] "b" "a" "c" "a" "b" dts_data(x_fct) #> [1] low  high low  #> Levels: low medium high length(x_long) #> [1] 50 x_long[1:2] #> Discrete time series of length 2 with state space A, B, C #>  B A try(dts(c("a", NA, "b"))) #> Error in validate_dts(x, vals) :  #>   discrete time series cannot contain missing values

Using dts directly useful mainly state space model deduced reliably series used estimate , common situation several series analysed state space. Let us consider household electricity consumption data set powerconsumption. vignette("covlmc"), active power discretised three levels. following function extracts discretised series weeks data set (character vector): consumption low week 33, August (probably holidays), high level never observed. model estimated week character vector therefore two states used week 35: specify state space dts, model knows high level exists: log likelihood now computed, value, \(-\infty\), tells us week 35 impossible according model week 33, high level never observed week. predicted probabilities include states state space, specified order (last row prediction state follows series, see predict.vlmc()): Notice new data (newdata loglikelihood() predict(), init simulate() sequence given find_sequence()) can given plain vector dts. cases, interpreted state space model: dts different state space accepted provided values belong state space model. instance, following call computes log likelihood week 34, high level also absent, model week 33: series factor, levels define state space, discretising directly cut() (without conversion character used ) also gives model three states: Finally, simulate() return dts vector type state space model (character vector), whose values taken state space. can converted dts state space follows:
code: power_levels <- c("low", "typical", "high") power_weeks <- function(weeks) {   pc <- powerconsumption[powerconsumption$week %in% weeks, ]   as.character(cut(pc$active_power,     breaks = c(0, 0.4, 2, 8),     labels = power_levels   )) } week_33 <- power_weeks(33) week_35 <- power_weeks(35) table(week_33) #> week_33 #>     low typical  #>     925      83 table(week_35) #> week_35 #>    high     low typical  #>      28     891      89 model_33_raw <- vlmc(week_33) states(model_33_raw) #> [1] "low"     "typical" try(loglikelihood(model_33_raw, newdata = week_35)) #> Error : x contains unknown states week_33_dts <- dts(week_33, vals = power_levels) model_33 <- vlmc(week_33_dts) model_33 #> VLMC context tree on low, typical, high [C++] #>  cutoff: 2.996 (quantile: 0.05) #>  Number of contexts: 42  #>  Maximum context length: 24 loglikelihood(model_33, newdata = week_35) #> 'log Lik.' -Inf (df= 84, nb obs.= 984, initial="truncated") predict(model_33, newdata = week_35[1:5], type = "probs") #>            low    typical high #> [1,] 0.9176587 0.08234127    0 #> [2,] 0.9155844 0.08441558    0 #> [3,] 0.9088757 0.09112426    0 #> [4,] 0.9009126 0.09908735    0 #> [5,] 0.8942029 0.10579710    0 #> [6,] 0.8847403 0.11525974    0 week_34_dts <- dts(power_weeks(34)) states(week_34_dts) #> [1] "low"     "typical" loglikelihood(model_33, newdata = week_34_dts) #> 'log Lik.' -201.5814 (df= 84, nb obs.= 984, initial="truncated") states(vlmc(factor(week_33, levels = power_levels))) #> [1] low     typical high    #> Levels: low typical high sim_33 <- simulate(model_33, 20, seed = 0) sim_33 #>  [1] "low"     "low"     "low"     "low"     "typical" "low"     "low"     #>  [8] "low"     "low"     "low"     "low"     "low"     "low"     "low"     #> [15] "low"     "low"     "low"     "low"     "typical" "low" dts(sim_33, vals = states(model_33)) #> Discrete time series of length 20 with state space low, typical, high #>  low low low low typical ...

code: best_elec_vlmc_aic <- as_vlmc(tune_vlmc(elec_dts, criterion = "AIC")) set.seed(0) vlmc_simul <- vector(mode = "list", 100) for (k in seq_along(vlmc_simul)) {   vlmc_simul[[k]] <- simulate(best_elec_vlmc_aic, nsim = length(elec_dts), init = elec_dts[1:2]) } set.seed(0) covlmc_simul <- vector(mode = "list", 100) for (k in seq_along(covlmc_simul)) {   covlmc_simul[[k]] <- simulate(best_elec_covlmc_aic, nsim = length(elec_dts), covariate = elec_cov, init = elec_dts[1:2]) } longuest_high <- function(x) {   high_length <- rle(x == "high")   10 * max(high_length$lengths[high_length$values]) } lh_vlmc <- sapply(vlmc_simul, longuest_high) lh_covlmc <- sapply(covlmc_simul, longuest_high) lh <- data.frame(   time = c(lh_vlmc, lh_covlmc),   model = c(rep("VLMC", length(lh_vlmc)), rep("COVLMC", length(lh_covlmc))) ) ggplot(lh, aes(x = time, color = model)) +   geom_density() +   geom_rug(alpha = 0.5) +   geom_vline(xintercept = longuest_high(elec_dts), color = 3) elec_cov_long_days <- data.frame(day = (pc_week_5$hour >= 6 & pc_week_5$hour <= 20)) set.seed(0) covlmc_simul_ld <- vector(mode = "list", 100) for (k in seq_along(covlmc_simul_ld)) {   covlmc_simul_ld[[k]] <- simulate(best_elec_covlmc_aic, nsim = length(elec_dts), covariate = elec_cov_long_days, init = elec_dts[1:2]) } lh_covlmc_ld <- sapply(covlmc_simul_ld, longuest_high) day_time_effect <- data.frame(   time = c(lh_covlmc, lh_covlmc_ld),   `day length` = c(rep("Short days", length(lh_covlmc)), rep("Long days", length(lh_covlmc_ld))),   check.names = FALSE ) ggplot(day_time_effect, aes(x = time, color = `day length`)) +   geom_density() +   geom_rug(alpha = 0.5)

title: Fit a Variable Length Markov Chain with Covariates (COVLMC) — covlmc.default
text: model built using algorithm described Zanin Zambom et al. vlmc() approach, algorithm builds first context tree (see ctx_tree()). min_size parameter used compute actual number observations per context growing phase tree. computed min_size*(1+p*d)*(s-1) d length context (.k.. depth tree), s number states p number parameters associated one time step covariates (one per numerical logical covariate, number levels minus one per factor). corresponds ensuring min_size observations per parameter logistic regression estimation phase. logistic models fitted leaves tree: goal logistic model estimate conditional distribution next state time series given context (recent past time series) delayed versions covariates. pruning strategy used simplify models (mainly reduce time window associated covariates) tree . Parameters specified control used fine-tune behaviour algorithm.

title: Fit a Variable Length Markov Chain with Covariates (COVLMC) — covlmc.default
text: default, covlmc uses two different computing engines logistic models: time series two states, covlmc uses stats::glm() binomial family (stats::binomial()); time series least three states, covlmc uses VGAM::vglm() multinomial family (VGAM::multinomial()). possible replace stats::glm() VGAM::vglm() nnet::multinom() setting global option mixvlmc.predictive "multinom" (default value "glm"). engines estimate models, results always identical: stats::glm() VGAM::vglm() use iteratively reweighted least squares nnet::multinom() uses quasi-Newton optimisation. data context (almost) separable, instance value covariate determines next state, maximum likelihood coefficients infinite engines stop different (large) values. likelihoods remain close, coefficients can quite different likelihood ratio test whose p-value close alpha can lead different decisions, thus different models. stats::glm() VGAM::vglm() report warning converge mixvlmc.maxit iterations (see mixvlmc-package), nnet::multinom() . states never follow context data ignored model context, gives zero probability fewer coefficients. Similarly, levels factor covariates absent data context ignored: VGAM::vglm() reports coefficient stats::glm() nnet::multinom() report zero coefficient (instance text format draw.covlmc(); LaTeX format shows zero coefficients engines). engine used estimate COVLMC recorded model: also used estimate new logistic models needed prune.covlmc(), even option changed (warning). number parameters COVLMC, used stats::AIC() stats::BIC(), counts coefficients covariates actually estimated engine (consequence last point list ) intercepts: depend engine (see "Number parameters" section loglikelihood.covlmc()).

code: pc <- powerconsumption[powerconsumption$week == 5, ] rdts <- cut(pc$active_power, breaks = c(0, quantile(pc$active_power, probs = c(0.5, 1)))) rdts_cov <- data.frame(day_night = (pc$hour >= 7 & pc$hour <= 17)) m_cov <- covlmc(rdts, rdts_cov, min_size = 5) draw(m_cov) #> ▪ #> ├─ (0,1.34] #> │  ├─ (0,1.34] #> │  │  ├─ (0,1.34] ([ -2.813 • 2.178 ⁞ -4.449 ⁞ 2.418 ]) #> │  │  └─ (1.34,7.54] ([ -19.57 • 18.39 ]) #> │  └─ (1.34,7.54] (0.8649, 0.1351) #> └─ (1.34,7.54] (0.07341, 0.9266) cutoff(m_cov) #> [1] 0.02328831 0.01834317 ## raw values are slightly larger than the default ones cutoff(m_cov, raw = TRUE) - cutoff(m_cov) #> [1] 1.735114e-10 1.366673e-10 ## pruning with the largest cut off value draw(prune(m_cov, alpha = cutoff(m_cov)[1])) #> ▪ #> ├─ (0,1.34] #> │  ├─ (0,1.34] ([ -2.759 • 2.785 ⁞ -2.525 ]) #> │  └─ (1.34,7.54] (0.8649, 0.1351) #> └─ (1.34,7.54] (0.07341, 0.9266)

Two values supported: "glm" (default value): covlmc() uses stats::glm() binomial link (stats::binomial()) two-value state space, VGAM::vglm() multinomial link (VGAM::multinomial()) state space three values; "multinom": covlmc() uses nnet::multinom() cases. first option "glm" recommended stats::glm() VGAM::vglm() able detect deal degeneracy data set. results two options can differ, see "Logistic models" section covlmc(). mixvlmc.backend: specifies implementation used context tree construction ctx_tree(), vlmc() tune_vlmc(). Two values supported: "C++" (default value): corresponds C++ implementation, significantly faster R implementation. "R": corresponds original almost pure R implementation, whose context trees nested lists can processed R. implementations give models. covlmc() tune_covlmc() always use R implementation. mixvlmc.charset: specifies collection characters used display context trees "ascii art" using "text" format draw() related functions. title: Simulate a discrete time series for a VLMC with covariates — simulate.covlmc
code: pc <- powerconsumption[powerconsumption$week == 5, ] rdts <- cut(pc$active_power, breaks = c(0, quantile(pc$active_power, probs = c(0.5, 1)))) rdts_cov <- data.frame(day_night = (pc$hour >= 7 & pc$hour <= 17)) m_cov <- covlmc(rdts, rdts_cov, min_size = 5) # new week with daylight from 6:00 to 18:00 (144 observations per day, one # every 10 minutes) new_cov <- data.frame(   day_night = rep(c(rep(FALSE, 36), rep(TRUE, 72), rep(FALSE, 36)), times = 7) ) new_rdts <- simulate(m_cov, nrow(new_cov), seed = 0, covariate = new_cov) table(new_rdts) #> new_rdts #>    (0,1.34] (1.34,7.54]  #>         577         431  new_rdts_2 <- simulate(m_cov, nrow(new_cov), seed = 0, covariate = new_cov, init = rdts[1:10]) ## the simulated time series starts with the initial values identical(as.character(new_rdts_2[1:10]), as.character(rdts[1:10])) #> [1] TRUE
